Bot
BOT
noun (Gen Alpha slang)
Clipped from robot (from Czech robota, forced labor; Karel Capek’s play R.U.R., 1920). In games a bot is a computer-controlled player; when Fortnite added bots to new players’ lobbies in late 2019, Gen Alpha turned the word into an insult for a person who plays badly, predictably, or mindlessly — "you’re such a bot." It now means anyone judged clueless, and sits beside the related insult NPC.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Calling someone a bot means he plays like a computer — clumsy, predictable, easy to beat — or, more broadly, that he is clueless. "Bro is a bot" is a common Gen Alpha insult. The Christian observation: the insult works by turning a person into a machine, and Scripture forbids that move. Every person is made in God’s image: "So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him" (Gen 1:27). The same tongue that blesses God must not curse "men, which are made after the similitude of God" (Jas 3:9). To mock the weak player is to mock his Maker: "Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker" (Pro 17:5). A bot has no soul; the boy you call a bot does, and Christ died for him. Jesus warned that contempt is a matter of the heart: "whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire" (Mat 5:22). A father can tell a five-year-old: "A bot is a computer, not a person. People are made by God, so we never call them names like that — even if they’re not good at the game yet." And he can teach the older child to see the "bot" in the lobby as a beginner to help.

Webster 1828 Definition

Clip of robot; game AI player turned Gen Alpha insult (Fortnite, 2019) for a weak or clueless person — contempt that reduces an image-bearer to a machine.

BOT, n. (clip of robot; gaming usage; Gen Alpha insult, 2019–present) A computer-controlled player; hence, a person who plays badly or acts mindlessly. "Stop being a bot."

Related insults: NPC, noob, default.

Other senses: social-media bots (automated accounts); chatbots.

Decode for parents: a mild-sounding word that carries real contempt.

Key Scripture

Gen 1:27 — "So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them."

Jas 3:9 — "Therewith bless we God, even the Father; and therewith curse we men, which are made after the similitude of God."

Pro 17:5 — "Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker: and he that is glad at calamities shall not be unpunished."

Mat 5:22 — "But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment: and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council: but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire."

Modern Corruption

Bot turns a weaker player into a machine; Scripture says every person bears God’s image, and contempt for him reproaches his Maker.

expand to see more

Dehumanizing language is easy when the other person is an avatar. The insult "bot" is meant as light trash talk, but its logic is that the other player is not really a person — just code to be farmed. Children practice that logic in game lobbies and carry it to the lunch table, where the "bot" is the kid who is slow, awkward, or new.

Answer with the image of God. Teach that every player behind every screen is a person, and that our words toward the weak reveal our hearts. Replace the insult with a habit: help the beginner, say "good game," and remember that God is mindful of the clumsy too.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Czech robota (forced labor) → robot (Capek, 1920) → bot (computing; game AI) → Gen Alpha insult (2019).
